title: Reversing keeps the core rows; an auto-applied deposit blocks it
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user. That role holds every permission, including Part sales -> Create & Edit and Invoicing & payments -> Create & Edit.
  2. A test customer exists. If not: Customers -> New Customer, enter a name (e.g. "4 Star Truck Repair") and save.
  3. A test vendor exists to order parts from. If not: Parts -> Vendors -> New Vendor, enter a Name (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Parts Supply"), then Save & Close.
  4. Start a new part sale today (a sale started before this release handles cores the old way): Parts -> Part Sales -> New Part Sale, then select the customer.
  5. On the Parts tab click Add Part and fill the row: Description "Water Pump", Quantity 1, Vendor = the test vendor, Sell Price $517.55, and in the Core column a Core Charge of $79.99. Save the row.
  6. In that row's Actions column click Order and confirm. The row now shows Awaiting.
  7. Click Receive on the row; in the Receive parts dialog keep the full quantity and confirm. The part row reads Received and its core row offers Return Core in the Actions column.
  8. On the core row click Return Core. The core row shows the Returned badge, and the document gains a Core credit row of -$79.99.
  9. Click Create Invoice. In New Customer Payment record a payment for the full balance (Payment Method e.g. "Cash") and save. Do not just close the dialog: closing it without paying cancels the invoice.
  10. Then, on the Finance tab, find that payment in the payment history and reverse it. The sale stays invoiced, with no payment applied.
  11. A second part sale built the same way (new sale, core line, Order, Receive) but NOT returned. Before invoicing, take a deposit for its full total: read the Total on the Finance tab (e.g. $627.42), then Add Deposit for that amount and Record Deposit.
  12. Click Create Invoice on the second sale. The deposit applies automatically; if New Customer Payment opens, it shows nothing left to pay - close it.
custom_steps:
1. On the first invoiced sale (no payment), reverse the invoice (the Reverse invoice action).
  2. Confirm the invoice and its customer transaction are deleted and the sale returns to its rows.
  3. Read whether the Core charge and Core credit rows are still present, and whether the Core credit blocked the reversal.
  4. On the second sale (deposit applied at invoicing), try to reverse the invoice and read the result.
  5. In that sale's payment history, reverse the payment that applied the deposit, then read the deposit's status on the sale.
  6. Reverse the invoice now; then click Create Invoice again and read whether the deposit is applied again.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Reversing the first invoice deletes the invoice and its customer transaction and the sale returns to the rows it was carrying: the Core charge stands and, if the return still stands, so does the Core credit.
  • The Core credit row does not block the reversal; the Core credit is a row on the document, not a customer credit.
  • On the second sale the reversal is refused while the automatically applied deposit is applied, as on a work order.
  • After reversing that payment the deposit shows Held on the sale, and the invoice can then be reversed.
  • The next invoice applies the deposit again.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-9667 (Founder Mode Batch #1); story SV-10262 (Story 1, Return a core on a part sale); Part Sales Update v1 PRD (Confluence 867434569), Story 1; design canvas boards Cores_*/Document_*; read 5 Oct 2026 (specification edited that day). Source-verified 5 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R19: “Reversing a part sale invoice deletes the invoice and its customer transaction, and the sale returns to the rows it was carrying: the core charge stands and, if the return still stands, so does its credit. The Core credit row does not block the reversal, because reversal is refused only when a payment is applied”
  • S1-R19: “It is a row on the document, not a customer credit”
  • S1-R19: “A deposit applied automatically at invoicing (S8-R5) is a payment, so the reversal is refused while it is applied, exactly as on a work order”
  • S1-R19: “Staff first reverse the payment that applied it; the deposit returns to Held on the sale, the invoice can then be reversed”
  • S1-R19: “the next invoice applies the deposit again”
